target_customer: Marketing and data teams at mid-size and large companies with a cloud data warehouse
problem: Customer data sits in the warehouse while marketing and sales tools work from stale copies; teams need that warehouse data synced into operational tools and used to personalize campaigns.
business_model: B2B SaaS with usage and platform-tier pricing (reverse ETL, composable CDP, AI decisioning)
product_category: Reverse ETL, composable customer data platform and AI marketing

founders.name: Tejas Manohar
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as an early engineer at Segment; TechCrunch (February 2025) says he and Josh Curl worked together at Segment.

founders.name: Kashish Gupta
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch describes him as a machine learning specialist and a friend of Curl's.

founders.name: Josh Curl
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no bio; TechCrunch says he was a Segment colleague of Manohar.

technical_complexity.rationale: Syncing warehouse data to hundreds of SaaS APIs reliably, with diffing and scheduling at scale, is hard integration engineering but standard software for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations and customer audience definitions create lock-in once embedded, but the sync layer itself can be copied by rivals and warehouse vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Census, the closest rival, was acquired by Fivetran in May 2025 per a search summary; Hightouch stayed independent and moved up to a composable CDP and AI marketing platform.

market_need_then: Companies were centralizing data in cloud warehouses and needed that data in marketing and sales tools; no demand figures from 2019 were found. Series A coverage in 2021 noted about 60 connected tools.

branding.domain_note: Uses hightouch.com; earlier posts appear on hightouch.io, suggesting a .io period before the .com, but no source states how or when the .com was obtained.

identity.visual_style: August 2025 redesign with expanded color palette and more approachable design for marketers
identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned toward marketers: clarity and speed rather than data-team patterns

rebrands.from: Data-heavy visual design aimed at data teams
rebrands.to: New visual language aimed at marketers
rebrands.why: Company blog says marketers use Hightouch differently than data teams

branding.community_and_virality: Company publishes a What's New series and appears on Redpoint InfraRed 100 lists; no merch or fan community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among data and marketing teams with strong customer logos and heavy trade press, but sources show no brand-driven growth beyond product category leadership.

pivots.from: Reverse ETL product for data teams
pivots.to: Composable CDP for marketers, then AI decisioning and agentic marketing
pivots.why: A Sacra summary says pure reverse ETL became too narrow; company site now lists the Agentic Marketing Platform and Composable CDP

outcome_analysis: Hightouch started as a reverse ETL tool and moved up to a composable CDP and AI marketing platform. It raised a 2.1 million seed in December 2020, 12.1 million Series A in July 2021, 40 million Series B at 450 million in November 2021, an 80 million Series C at 1.2 billion in February 2025 and a reported 150 million round at 2.75 billion in April 2026, while reaching about 100 million ARR per a TechCrunch headline. It acquired HeadsUp in 2023 and Workbase in 2022.
notes: Competitor list left empty: searches found Census (YC, seed announced May 2020), Segment, Grouparoo and RudderStack as rivals, but no source dated near the 2019 batch was opened. Series B and Series C details come partly from search summaries; the Series D 2.75B figure comes from a teaser on the Hightouch blog plus a WSJ headline on the YC page (April 29, 2026), and an aggregator lists 2.8B. Seed amount from a TechCrunch URL slug and VentureBeat and Seedtable via search summary; seed investors not stated. The 2023 38M round has no lead named. A 2025-07 Series C extension amount is undisclosed (one source says 12M). Founding year differs by source: 2018 (Seedtable) and 2019. Education not found. Layoff search found none; acquisitions found: Workbase (April 2022), HeadsUp (November 2023), Strata (date unknown).
